"Venerable sir, please accept it! Baddhananda replied,
"I ought not to accept this price for the robe."
"If you obtain a pure robe, you should receive and maintain it with your own hands.
The messenger said:
"Venerable Sir!"
"Is there anyone in charge?
Vāḍanada then pointed out the location.
The messenger went to the person in charge and said:
"A certain high minister has sent this value of cloth for Vāṇada. Please accept it and make [a robe] for him;
when he comes to collect it, you may give it to him.
Once the messenger had delivered it, he returned to Vāṇada’s place and said:
"I have already given the person in charge whom the Venerable One pointed out.
If the Venerable One requires robes, you may go and take them.
Having said this, he returned.
Some time later, the minister again sent a messenger to inquire of Baddhālī:
"Recently I dispatched a messenger to deliver the price for robes to a certain official; has the Venerable One already put on these robes?"
Bhadananda said, "I have not yet taken hold of it.
When he returned and reported this, the minister thought to himself:
"I have had this robe made for a long time, yet I still have not taken it; surely you have treated my robe with disdain, which is why this has come to pass.
He then sent a messenger again to speak to Baddhananda, saying:
"I have sent the robe to you for a long time; for what reason do you not wear it?"
"If you do not need it, you may return it to me. Upananda replied,
"I have a great need for it!"
Thereupon, at an improper time, he went to the place of the steward and said, "I now require robes; please give them to me. He replied:
“Wait a moment; there is a great assembly now, and I ought to attend it. If I do not arrive on time, I shall be fined five hundred pieces of gold.
Upananda said, “You have always been faithful and joyful, and diligent in your devotion to the Dharma.”
"Why do you suddenly concern yourself with worldly affairs today?
Upon hearing these words, he thought to himself:
"Even if I am punished, I must certainly deliver the robe before I depart."
He immediately prepared and gave it to him.
When the task was finished, he galloped back as fast as the stars move, but arrived late; the others asked him, "Why have you come so late?"
He replied, "Bhadanta Ananda requested a robe; I prepared it and returned it to him, which is why this has come to pass. Everyone said:
"Because he has slighted the communal regulations for the sake of a single bhikṣu, the principle of the matter allows no leniency! He was then punished.
Having received the punishment, he spoke with resentment:
"The śramaṇas, sons of the Śākyas, claim for themselves that they possess the Way and benefit all beings;
yet now they have instead caused me to receive this punishment.
Those who did not believe in or delight in the Buddha-dharma all spoke thus:
"Because you have placed your faith and respect in this śramaṇa, you have incurred this heavy punishment.
If you continue to associate with him, it shall be even more severe than this.
Thus, his ill repute spread throughout the city of Śrāvastī.
When the elder bhikṣus heard of this, they censured him in various ways and brought him to the Buddha’s presence to report the matter to the Buddha.
The Buddha, on account of this matter, assembled the community of bhikṣus and asked Upananda:
"Is it true that you did so?"
He replied, “It is true,
World-Honored One.”
After the Buddha had rebuked them in various ways, he addressed the bhikṣus:
"For ten reasons, I shall establish a precept for the bhikṣus. From now on, this precept should be recited as follows:
'If a king, a great minister, a brāhmaṇa, or a householder, for the sake of a bhikṣu, sends a messenger to deliver the value of a robe.'"
The messenger went to where the bhikṣu was and said:
"Venerable sir!
That king, the great ministers, the brahmins, and the householders have sent this value for robes."
"Venerable sir, please accept it! The bhikṣu says:
"I should not accept the price for a robe."
"If you obtain a pure robe, you should receive and maintain it with your own hands.
He then said, "Venerable Sir!"
"Is there anyone in charge?
The bhikṣu then pointed out the location, and the messenger went to the place where the official was and said:
"A certain king or great minister has sent this value of cloth for a certain bhikṣu."
"You act as the recipient; take it and give it to him.
Once the messenger had given it, he returned to the bhikṣu and said, "Venerable sir, the person designated by you as the steward has already been provided with it."
"Venerable sir, you need robes; you may go and take them.
The bhikṣu went to the person in charge two or three times and said:
"I need robes; I need robes."
If he succeeds, it is well;
if not, he should go before the official four times, five times, or six times, standing silently in attendance. If he succeeds, it is well.
If one seeks it beyond this limit, it is a *niḥsargika-pāyattika*.
If the robe is not obtained, one should go to the place from which the messenger came, either going there oneself or sending a messenger, and say:
"The price for a robe was sent by you for the sake of a certain bhikṣu; that bhikṣu has ultimately not received it."
"You must go back and seek it yourself; do not let it be lost!
Such is the proper course of action.
It is the same for bhikṣuṇīs as well.
For the śikṣamāṇā, śrāmaṇera, and śrāmaṇerī, this concludes the tenth section on the *duṣkṛta* offense.
At that time, the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī.
Then, the community of monks received a large amount of thread as an offering and divided it among themselves.

The bhikṣus used [the cloth] to sew saṃghāṭī robes, uttarāsaṅga robes, antaravāsaka robes, and all other garments; they also made waist-bands, meditation belts, and even door-knots, yet it was still not exhausted.
At that time, the group of six bhikṣus hired weavers to weave a robe for them; when there was still some thread remaining, they hired them again to weave another.
When the thread was insufficient, they went out to beg for it, and the elders and householders all gave it to them.
Thereupon, the group of six bhikṣus thought to themselves:
"We have gained a great benefit; from now on, we shall constantly engage in this work alone.
They then solicited thread in great quantities and hired all the weavers to weave for them.
At that time, there was a householder who went to a weaver and hired him to weave a robe.
The weaver replied, "I have already promised to provide one for a bhikṣu; I cannot make another."
He went everywhere else, and it was the same in all places.
Thereupon, the householder spoke with anger and reproach:
"The śramaṇas, sons of the Śākyas, are said to have few desires and to know contentment; yet now they employ all the weavers, showing no sense of satiety."
"What difference is there between you and those who are greedy for worldly things?
You lack the conduct of a śramaṇa and have destroyed the dharma of a śramaṇa!
When the elder bhikṣus heard this, they rebuked him in various ways and reported the matter to the Buddha.
The Buddha, on account of this matter, assembled the community of bhikṣus and asked the group of six bhikṣus:
"Is it true that you did so? They replied:
"It is truly so,
World-Honored One!
After the Buddha had rebuked him in various ways, he addressed the bhikṣus:
"For ten reasons, I establish this precept for the bhikṣus. From now on, this precept should be recited as follows:
'If a bhikṣu personally begs for thread and hires a weaver to weave it into a robe, it is a *niḥsargika-pāyattika*.'"
The same applies to bhikṣuṇīs.
For śikṣamāṇās, śrāmaṇeras, and śrāmaṇerīs, it is a duṣkṛta. [Section Eleven concludes.
The Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī.
At that time, Upananda frequently visited the home of a certain merchant, preaching the Dharma and treating his illnesses.
The merchant said to his wife, "Upananda has been kind to me;
you may use this thread to hire a weaver to make a robe for him, and I shall repay you when I return."
After he had departed, the wife took the thread to a weaver and hired him to weave it, saying:
"Measure it so that it is sufficient; do not let it be too short or too long."
When Pūraṇa Kāśyapa heard this, he went immediately to her house.
The wife came out to greet him and said, "My husband instructed me to make a robe for the Venerable One; I have already hired someone to make it."
Bhadanta said, "Whom did you hire to do it? He replied:
"Such-and-such. Then, Vāḷananda went to the weaver's place and said to him, "Do you know?"
"This robe is being made for me; you must weave it well so that it is fine and wide, and I shall privately reward you with a small amount.
The weaver replied, "That woman told me to calculate the requirements so they would be sufficient; how can I now make it both fine and wide?"
Bhadanta said, "Simply weave it well;
if the thread should run short, go and ask for more on my behalf, and I shall certainly provide it to you.
Following these instructions, the weaver used up all the material and went to request more.
The merchant’s wife said,
“I told you beforehand that I would provide enough after careful calculation.
Why do you ask for more again?”
The weaver related the matter in full, and the wife then gave him the cloth.
When the merchant returned from his journey, he asked his wife, "I previously instructed you to make a robe for Baddhālita; have you finished it yet?"
He replied, "It has been done.
[The other said,] "Bring it here so that we may see it."
The wife immediately took it out and showed it to him; the cloth was extremely fine and exquisite.
He asked, "With such a small amount of thread, how could it have come to this? She replied:
“Bhadrananda came again to take thread; that is why this happened.
The merchants then scolded him, saying:
“Bhadrananda is difficult to support and difficult to satisfy; he knows no contentment.”
"According to my original intention, this robe is worth many times its value!
Although there was previously some kindness, it has now ceased!
He then refused to give it to him, and thus a bad reputation spread far and wide.
When the elder bhikṣus heard of this, they rebuked him in various ways and brought him to the Buddha’s presence to report the matter to the Buddha.
The Buddha, on account of this matter, assembled the community of bhikṣus and asked Upananda:
"Is it true that you did this?"
He replied, “It is indeed so,
World-Honored One!”
After the Buddha had rebuked them in various ways, he addressed the bhikṣus:
"For ten reasons, I shall establish a precept for the bhikṣus. From now on, this precept should be recited as follows:
'If a householder or a householder’s wife has a weaver weave a robe for a bhikṣu.'"
Without having first been invited to choose his own requisites, that bhikṣu went to the weaver’s place and spoke thus: "Do you know?
This robe is being made for me; weave it well for me, making it extremely fine and wide, and I shall reward you accordingly."
"If, later, one should give him a meal or the value of a meal, and he receives it, it is a *naiḥsargika-pāyattika* offense.
It is the same for a bhikṣuṇī.
The *śikṣamāṇā*, *śrāmaṇera*, and *śrāmaṇerī* [commit] a *duṣkṛta* offense; the twelve [cases] are concluded.
The Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī.
At that time, Upananda said to his disciple Dharma:
"I now wish to travel with you to the kingdom of Kośala.
Dharma said, "It is cold there and I have no clothes; I cannot go."
Bhadanta said, "If you can leave, I shall give you this robe. Dharma replied:
"Give me my robe first, and only then shall I depart. He then gave it to him.
Having received the robe, he nevertheless refused to go.
Bhadanta said: "You said that once you had obtained the robe, you would depart; why have you obtained the robe and yet still refuse to go?
If you cannot go, return the robe to me."
Dharma said, "The teacher has already accepted the gift; why do you ask for it again? Upananda replied:
"I did not give you this out of charity; rather, I gave it to you because I wished to travel together with you!
If you do not go now, by what reasoning can you refuse to return it to me?"
He then forcibly seized it from her, whereupon she cried out loudly.
An elder bhikṣu asked, "Why are you crying?"
He replied, "The teacher has taken my robe!
The bhikṣus then reproached Upananda in various ways:
“How is it that a bhikṣu forcibly takes another’s robe?
He replied, “I wished to travel together with him to the kingdom of Kośala, and I intended to hire him by means of this robe.”
"Once he had obtained the robe, he refused to leave; therefore, we took it from him, not by means of forceful seizure.

He then took the two men with him to the Buddha’s dwelling and reported the matter to the Buddha.

He replied, “It is indeed so,
World-Honored One.”
The Buddha asked Dharma again,

"It is truly so,
World-Honored One!
After the Buddha had reproved the two bhikṣus in various ways, he addressed the bhikṣus:
"For ten reasons, I establish this precept for the bhikṣus. From now on, this precept should be recited as follows:

At that time, the group of six bhikṣus gave robes to other bhikṣus and then had śrāmaṇeras and park-keepers seize them back.
The bhikṣus asked them,

He replied, "I have heard it;

"What difference is there between taking it oneself and instructing another to do so?
Having rebuked them in various ways, they reported the matter to the Buddha.
The Buddha, on account of this matter, assembled the community of bhikṣus and questioned the group of six bhikṣus:

“[This constitutes] a *niḥsargika-pāyattika* offense. It is the same for a bhikṣuṇī.
